speaker: expecting_mother
quote: It feels like they are just trying to make this as hard as possible on me to find any accommodations or work with me through this extremely rough time. Almost like they want me to quit to avoid firing me and potentially having to pay unemployment.
context: Early second trimester, small medical office employer resisting accommodations.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: after another horrible night of pelvic pain and of course our toddler wanting water at 2 in the middle of the night and then crawling up in our bed, forcing me to go out to the sofa and spend the rest of the night there.
context: 34 weeks with her second, the night before a forgotten Mother's Day.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: My husband doesn’t even notice that our toddler has left the bed, or that I slept on the sofa. I just sit there waiting for him to wake up, at 8 he gets up. No breakfast, no flowers, nothing.
context: Up since 5:30 with the toddler while her husband slept through.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: there’s a long history of him “accidentally” favouring his mum and sisters wants and needs over mine because he hasn’t wanted to cause issues with them
context: Overdue, living in her husband's country, hurt that nobody marked Mother's Day.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I feel guilty calling off work a lot or coming in late, I don’t have energy to do this especially during the morning.
context: 24 weeks, a manager moved from nights to day shift, providing for herself without family nearby.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Unfortunately, I don’t think I can get a promotion with this impression I’m giving off. I don’t seem reliable at this time.
context: On how pregnancy symptoms look at work.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m actually considering going to classes to feel some type of community around me and a doula that support home birth as I want it to be intimate and natural as possible. I always have bad experiences with doctors and nurses not really caring about how I feel and just go by what they assume and expect.
context: Alone, considering classes for community and a doula after bad experiences with clinicians.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I made it very clear that this wouldn’t be a holiday visit And we wont be going to coffee places, brunches etc. I’ll most likely be exhausted, and I was hoping to have someone around to help with little things like watching the baby while I shower, run to the shop for groceries, or simply get a bit of rest.
context: First pregnancy, due in November, no family nearby except a sister asked to help after the birth.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: she contacted me and asked if she and her fiancé could come around my due date so they could attend a concert, and that they could both help with the baby. Honestly, that caught me off guard because it’s not what we originally discussed. Also, I have no idea when I’ll actually give birth
context: The sister's visit turned into a couple's trip timed to the due date.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: What was it like when you first came home from the hospital? Would you have wanted extra people staying in the house during those first few weeks, or would that have felt like more stress than help?
context: Asking experienced mothers whether house guests help or add stress after the birth.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: when I hit my second trimester I felt like a new woman and started feeling better as people say but I'm now 18 weeks and I have had the worst morning sickness since 17 weeks. What?!
context: UK, 18 weeks, sickness returned after the promised second-trimester relief.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: My consultant gave me anti sickness medication but then told me I can't drive with them and they'll make me very dizzy so I haven't taken them yet because this will interfere with work
context: Choosing between medication and getting to work.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I start with a simple idea and then I'm suddenly planning outfits, color palettes, props, locations, and trying to make it into a whole production.
context: 22 weeks, undecided about maternity photos and wary of a project. Possibly AI-structured post.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: He didn’t really want to talk through/hear about the breathing techniques I’d been reading about and was instead telling me anecdotes I didn’t really have headspace for by way of distraction.
context: UK, after a night at the assessment unit that previewed labour; her partner was agitated.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m terrified we are going to just get on each other’s nerves when I’m in labour - it worries me he’s not looked into any of the breathing techniques and massages that I might find useful.
context: Her partner hasn't prepared for his role in labour.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: How prepared are other people’s birth partners? Are you doing any prep together? Or expecting they will do anything independently? And is there anything anyone can recommend to get us both on the same page?
context: Asking how other couples prepare the birth partner.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I don’t think he deals with being unable to be in control of situations very well and generally holds medicine in higher regard than the hyponobirthing techniques Im interested in utilising.
context: Her partner, from a medical background, sceptical of the hypnobirthing she is learning.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote:
Mainly from books, I’m reading the hyponobirthing book by Siobhan Miller at the moment and have read pregnancy, bump and beyond, also just thinking about techniques from yoga classes I’ve been to. 

Weirdly unlike others, our NCT classes didn’t cover things like breathing techniques or positions for birth, more focused on setting the mood of the room from a sensory perspective
context: Where she learned her techniques; the NCT course left out breathing and positions.

speaker: new_mother
quote: For some reason I also couldn’t trust anyone else to look after my baby, even with in laws/own parents as I had bad experience them crossing my boundaries before and after giving birth.
context: Five weeks after the birth, too drained to book her own doctor's appointment.

speaker: new_mother
quote: talking to my husband about It doesnt change anything as he does not understand the feeling of giving birth and what happens after it.
context: Five weeks after the birth, recovering and feeling alone with it.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Is it weird that I was asked for a selfie of me pregnant?.. Of course, I’m 6 months and you still can’t really tell when I’m clothed. It just rubbed me the wrong way and crossed a small boundary?
context: First pregnancy, six months; a distant aunt asked for a pregnant selfie.
